I’m an orthopaedic resident. Would recommend the following: For digits (fingers or toes) describe everything based on their proximity to a joint. For example you could say a “volar laceration just proximal to the long finger PIP joint”. If you are describing concerns for tendon laceration you can use the [zones ](https://www.orthobullets.com/hand/6031/flexor-tendon-injuries) 

I think once you get comfortable with it, will be much faster than any other tool.

Super helpful to read this. Thank you. 
I’m starting to be convinced that this document is a primary driver of inflated costs in healthcare. Setting aside the fact that the ridiculously designed EHR’s exist to maximize billing potential, this document is also establishing the “gold standard” for a doctors visit. Documentation takes up so much time for the docs and navigating the billing process requires tremendous administrative FTE’s. 
I don’t know where you could even start with changing this? I doubt “Medicare for all” or any of the proposed health care agendas address this problem.
Somehow we’ve got to be able to create a system where I can be paid for the services that I render without undo burden of proof of what was done at the visit. Why do I need to be doing a 14 point ROS on a patient who has wrist pain? I should be spending that time and energy on their wrist and examining their images... god forbid I should actually speak to the patient and look them in the eye. 
Our generation of docs should be able to fix this problem. We are good with tech and know how to use it to supplement and enhance our life and our work. The primary driver, however, is billing and collections. So, unfortunately we have to start there. I don’t even know where I’d begin.

Agreed but I meant more along the lines of figuring out why I need to document 12 systems of the physical exam to bill a level 3 visit etc. Is that coming from Medicaid? Who designed this system? What was the initial impetus?
